utterances.text: Now, at some point in time on the 13th, did some buses and trucks arrive at the warehouse to transport you and other Muslim men to another location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Yes. Six buses arrived and then the Serb soldiers gave orders that we should get up and form a line one by one, because vehicles had come to transport us. We got up. When I got out, I saw six buses standing in the immediate vicinity. I could recognise Bauxite Milici and Centrotrans Sarajevo; those were the markings on the buses. I didn't recognise the other markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you say Bauxite Milici. Is Milici down in the Srebrenica municipality or in a different municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: It is a small town within the territory of Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I believe you also said there was another location, another mark on the bus that you noticed. What was the other mark that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Centrotrans, from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know the approximate time that these buses arrived on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: It was an hour before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you get on one of those buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: I did. I got on to a bus with Centrotrans Sarajevo written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many men besides yourself got on this Centrotrans bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: There were quite a number standing who didn't have enough seats to sit down, but I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So all the seats were filled on the bus and there were people standing in the aisle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, of the 296 men who were in the room of the warehouse where you were located, were you able to estimate the ages, the range of ages of the men who were in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: They were up to 60 and some were over 60. There was some who could hardly move with a stick.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you have an estimate as to the youngest person in the room, in your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: When we were coming out of the room into the bus, I didn't see any young people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you leave Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 1/E/1 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to indicate on this map, Witness N, for the benefit of the Judges, the direction that you travelled after you left Bratunac. There is a pointer -- there should be a pointer in front of you. Do you see the town of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do. I see it. Here it is [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you use your pointer and show the Judges your route of travel after you left Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: From Bratunac, we went towards Serbia [indicates]. We reached the Drina River. There's a bridge leading to Serbia. We didn't cross that bridge. So we went to the left, towards Zvornik [indicates]. We reached Zvornik, and then we went on to Karakaj. When we got to Karakaj, we turned left, when we got to a school and a large hall attached to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me stop you there for just a minute, Witness N.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, on Prosecutor's Exhibit 1/E/1, the witness pointed to a road that goes from Bratunac toward the Drina River, in a direction to the right side of the exhibit, and then follows the course of the river up through Zvornik to a town which is marked on the map, called Karakaj. Then the witness indicated that the bus turned left on a road that is marked, and there's a town on that which I, unfortunately, can't read off of the ELMO, but it looks to me like it begins with the letter "P."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness N, can you see the -- it looks like Petkovci, so that is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- the route that the witness travelled. Thank you, Witness N.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long did it take you from the time you left Bratunac to the time you got to this destination up near Petkovci, near this school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were there interruptions along the journey, along the route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Yes, there were several breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know -- strike that. Were you able to look around in your bus and see how many vehicles in your convoy were going north towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: No, I could only see the bus in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, on your bus, was there a guard or more than one guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: There were; one, only one guard, armed with an automatic rifle, wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this: Did you see any other buses that -- strike that. The vehicle that you saw in front of you, was it a bus or a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: A bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether that bus was -- how many people were in that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: One could see through the windows that there was a whole line of people standing in the aisle, that there wasn't enough room for everyone to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could I have that Exhibit 1/E/1 placed back on the ELMO, please, because I may have indicated incorrectly the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do, please, Witness N, again take that pointer and -- take your pointer and could you tell me when you got to the town of Karakaj. There appear on that diagram to be two roads; one below the town of Karakaj and one directly above the town of Karakaj. Do you know which of those two roads you took or do you merely recall turning left near the town of Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: I just remember that we turned left. It was night-time, and the windows of the buses were not very clean, so one couldn't know, and I'm not very familiar with the area either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, very much. Mr. President, we normally break at this time. I'm prepared to continue or to take a break at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think we need to adjourn. It is time. Shall we adjourn. Yes, Mr. Visnjic, you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not linked to this witness, but if you have decided that we should adjourn -- but reviewing the transcript on page 94 line 7, the last answer given by the previous witness, Witness M, and his last answer to Judge Wald's question. I think during the translation, and I must say that we all found the witness rather hard to follow, I think that during the translation, an error was made, so that the answer of that witness differs from the meaning in the transcript. I intervened with the interpreters, and they will probably be correcting the transcript. So I wish to make this formal objection so that it shall be registered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, thank you very much for drawing our attention to this problem. What we are going to do is that we are going to send the audio and visual tape to the translation section. The translation section will check, and if the translation is not correct, doesn't correspond to the original, then the transcript will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. Before adjourning, Mr. Harmon, in order to see how we are going to work until the end of the week, where do we stand in relation to the witnesses here present in The Hague. Are we going to have a chance to hear them? Are we running the risk of leaving a witness from the end of the week until I don't know when we meet again. So could you give us some information, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We anticipate completing the testimonies of the witnesses, of all of the witnesses who are here at The Hague, by Friday. In fact, we may end up short of time in which case, we are prepared to present different types of evidence to the Chamber to complete the trial day. We have three witnesses remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What I would like to avoid is to have witnesses whom we have to send back because we can't hear them or to have a witness who would have to be half finished. As it is 2.30, if you have other evidence in addition to witnesses, it would be a good idea to present that evidence to make use of the time. As you know, we have a Status Conference tomorrow at quarter past two. Perhaps I need to warn the interpreters that we may be working a quarter of an hour longer tomorrow. That's enough for today. Witness N, you will stay here. We will be continuing your testimony tomorrow. I hope you will have a restful evening.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS N
utterances.text: at 2.33 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of April, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
